svg.title: DDIA 11 · BATCH PROCESSING: sketchnote
svg.text: Read a large immutable input, compute, write a new output. Failures
are cheap: just run it again.
Sort by count and take the top 5. Six tiny programs, composed
through one uniform interface: a stream of lines.
task preempted or failed? run it again: inputs never change
Orchestrator (Airflow) runs the DAG; scheduler + resource
manager place tasks; executors read and write object storage.
Each reducer sees all values for its keys together, aggregates
them, and writes output files. If a task fails, just rerun that
Small table? BROADCAST it to every mapper (in-memory hash)
Broadcast hash join: if one side is small (a hotel dimension
table), load it into each mapper's memory. No shuffle is needed.
MapReduce: every stage writes to HDFS (3× replicated)
Spark / Flink: one DAG, intermediate state in memory
Dataflow engines run the whole workflow as one DAG and
Most jobs are now written in SQL or
DataFrames; MapReduce lives on as the shuffle.
The frontier queue feeds fetchers. Text extraction and dedup run as batch (Spark) over S3. Re-runnable because raw pages are stored immutably.
Nightly batch over the event log in S3 or the warehouse. The streaming path gives fast approximate results and batch gives exact ones (Ch 12, Lambda).
"How do you rebuild the search index?"
Batch-build a new index from the source of truth, then atomically switch the alias. Old index kept for rollback.
"Raw events land immutably in S3, partitioned by date. Any derived table can be recomputed from them, which is our safety net for bugs."
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.
